cards.art: yellow rabbit painting CORPORATE REALITY with giant brush
cards.lore: You are playing a game about playing a game. Try to keep up.
cards.name: The Great Kayfabe Improv Komedy SKETCHBOOK
cards.power: Print. Cut. Sabotage reality.

cards.art: yellow rabbit punching alarm clock in wrestling ring
cards.lore: No board. No pawns. No manual thicker than your wrist. That was a design decision, not laziness. Probably.
cards.name: Uncle FrizzleBob
cards.power: Destroy this book. Cut the cards. Shuffle them. See what happens.

cards.art: raccoons in luchador masks summoning character around ceremonial fire
cards.lore: The Intro isn't a character sheet. It's a promise. Say it like you mean it—the story starts the moment you commit.
cards.name: The Intro Ritual
cards.power: Name it. Claim it. Power it. Show us what this Power does to reality right now.

cards.art: punk iguana burning rulebook on stage, one finger raised
cards.lore: Kayfabe means the fiction is real. Bizarro means the permission to be strange, wrong, and surprising on purpose.
cards.name: The Golden Rule of Bizarro
cards.power: Perform it. Don't calculate it. Play the contradiction.

cards.art: sloth in armchair reading newspaper, absolute stasis
cards.lore: [Lore text degraded in PDF — OCR artifact on source file. Corrected: duration-based mundanity constraint.]
cards.name: The Boring Stasis
cards.power: Play this to force the current storyteller to describe a completely mundane, ordinary routine for exactly one minute.

cards.art: rhinoceros crashing through wall at sloth in armchair, both surprised
cards.lore: A story goes nowhere until the hero gets in trouble. Break the routine. Present a mystery that must be solved.
cards.name: The Sudden Tilt
cards.power: Play this to drastically change the relationship between two characters. Introduce a massive, unignorable problem.

cards.art: hedgehog surrounded by dynamite pointing at random object, explosion imminent
cards.lore: Open your mouth and allow anything to come out. Spontaneity is breaking the social conditioning that keeps you nice, safe, and boring.
cards.name: The Spontaneous Spark
cards.power: The active player must point to an object in the room and call it the first bizarre thing that comes to mind, incorporating it into the story instantly.

cards.art: black raven returning with bloodied sword to confused scene
cards.lore: Make the audience feel like you planned this from the very beginning. You didn't. But you gave yourself the details to steal later.
cards.name: The Reincorporation
cards.power: Play this to bring back an object, phrase, or character from the very first turn to instantly resolve the current conflict.

cards.art: badger behind NO signs in military helmet, arms crossed
cards.lore: Defense mechanisms that keep you safe in the real world make you absolutely terrible at games. Blocking kills the journey.
cards.name: The Brick-Wall Blocker
cards.power: Play this to completely reject another player's narrative offer. The story stops dead.

cards.art: possum under single spotlight, sweating, refusing to move
cards.lore: If you don't make a choice, nobody can tell you you're wrong. Why define the object when you can just play dead?
cards.name: The Waffling Wimp
cards.power: Refuse to define what is happening in the scene. Stall the narrative indefinitely out of fear of being judged.

cards.art: tabby cat knocking water glass onto brilliant narrative premise mid-setup
cards.lore: I'm going to light a fire! Oh wait, the rain came and put it out. Crisis averted, story ruined.
cards.name: The Smug Canceler
cards.power: Set up a brilliant narrative premise, then instantly wrap it in a bow and throw it in the trash before anyone else can interact with it.

cards.art: vulture under rain cloud at birthday cake, thumbs down
cards.lore: No, I won't go to Grandma's. It's raining, the woods are dark, and she smells funny. Negative answers kill your partner's ideas.
cards.name: The Negative Nancy
cards.power: Force the narrative to reject a gift or idea, but demand the active player continues the story anyway.

cards.art: beaver buried in red tape and requisition forms, can't see the bridge
cards.lore: You aren't building a bridge, you're building a cage. Unnecessary steps ensure nobody ever has to be emotionally changed.
cards.name: The Bureaucratic Bridger
cards.power: Play this to force the current storyteller to describe three utterly irrelevant objects before they are allowed to finish their scene.

cards.art: hedgehog curling at crossroads while high-stakes moment passes
cards.lore: What are you going to say to him? I don't know, I'll think about it. Postponing a good idea to protect your ego.
cards.name: The Hedging Hedgehog
cards.power: Push a vital, high-stakes decision to the next player's turn so you don't have to take the creative risk yourself.

cards.art: squirrel abandoning Excalibur mid-extraction to chase shiny acorn
cards.lore: Why hunt the Great Moose when we can stop at a diner and gossip for twenty minutes? The audience feels cheated.
cards.name: The Sidetracking Squirrel
cards.power: Hijack the Quest for a meaningless coffee break. Derail the main objective to discuss the weather.

cards.art: lemur on exercise wheel with internal monologue scrolling on rim
cards.lore: Picking violets, then roses, then daffodils, then berries... a brilliant strategy to avoid anything actually happening.
cards.name: The Looping Lemur
cards.power: Repeat the exact same action from the previous turn without advancing the plot or changing the emotional stakes.

cards.art: ostrich burying head in spaghetti noodles while wearing VR glasses in forest
cards.lore: Please don't be clever. Be as boring as you possibly can. Trying to be original just derails the world we built together.
cards.name: The "Original" Ostrich
cards.power: Derail the established genre entirely with a desperate, unearned attempt to look incredibly clever and avant-garde.

cards.art: hyena on burning drum kit delivering rimshot pun to emotional scene
cards.lore: Oh, what a grave situation! A joke is just a protective mechanism so the improviser doesn't have to experience real change.
cards.name: The Cheap Gagger
cards.power: Tell a terrible pun or one-liner to instantly escape a high-stakes, emotionally vulnerable scene.

cards.art: goose speaking into tin-can phone about absent parties, conflict visibly present and ignored
cards.lore: Talking about things that have already happened so you don't have to face the conflict standing right in front of you.
cards.name: The Gossip Goose
cards.power: Spend your entire turn talking exclusively about a character or event that is not currently present on the Stage.

cards.art: koala melded onto bear, dripping same paint colors, no friction possible
cards.lore: I paint in exactly the same style! We should collaborate! Congratulations, you're playing nicely and the story is dead.
cards.name: The Clingy Joiner
cards.power: Agree with the active player so hard, and with such identical emotional response, that further conflict becomes impossible.

cards.art: bulldog in suit perfectly still, color-splash behind, other player visibly folding
cards.lore: Status has nothing to do with occupation. It is a fluid game of power. I am still, therefore I am in charge.
cards.name: The High-Status Hound
cards.power: You may not move your head while speaking this turn. Force the player next to you to break eye contact first.

cards.art: nervous shrew in glasses fidgeting under spotlight, audience hearts visibly growing
cards.lore: Toes pointing in. Shoulders hunched. Hands drifting to the face. The epitome of the low-status climb.
cards.name: The Low-Status Shrew
cards.power: Fidget, giggle, and touch your face constantly. You automatically lose the current argument, but win the audience's sympathy.

cards.art: pig in overalls pointing at lion in sports car with parking ticket
cards.lore: We expect the high-status cop to pull over the low-status driver. Reversing it is where the comedy lives.
cards.name: The Status Swap
cards.power: Instantly reverse the power dynamic of the current Stage. The lowest character becomes the highest, and vice versa.

cards.art: peacock in full display slowly sinking into mud as scene progresses
cards.lore: Tragedy is the high character falling. Comedy is the low character climbing. All drama is just a status seesaw.
cards.name: The Status Transition
cards.power: Start your scene as the absolute, undisputed boss. End your scene humiliated in the metaphorical mud.

cards.art: exploding d20 with omega symbol, numbers and dramatic weight radiating
cards.lore: A story compass, not a countdown. As it rises, the dramatic weight shifts. You decide when to push hard or let it breathe.
cards.name: The Quest Die
cards.power: Advance the narrative arc from Akt I (Setup) to the Ordeal, and finally to the Finale.

cards.art: multicolour dice cube melting with comedy/tragedy masks on faces
cards.lore: The Mode is a frame, not a cage. If it creates a contradiction with your story—that is the story. Play the contradiction.
cards.name: The Story-Mode Die
cards.power: Roll to force a strict narrative genre constraint on the current turn. You must commit to the tone.

cards.art: two bears falling backward into each other blindfolded, thumbs up
cards.lore: The number one reason we practice is trust. I know that when I step on stage, they have my back, and I have theirs.
cards.name: The Trust Fall
cards.power: Accept the most absurd, logic-breaking narrative offer given to you without a single moment of hesitation.

cards.art: crowd of meerkats leaning forward in wide-eyed delight
cards.lore: We can make ourselves laugh all day long, but ultimately, the chaos demands a witness. We need someone to watch the work.
cards.name: The Willing Audience
cards.power: Call KayfaBINGO! on another player's move to validate a perfect, spontaneous narrative beat.

cards.art: elephant holding red sad balloon in rain, genuinely crying
cards.lore: Loss is real. Push forward anyway. Let the tragedy breathe.
cards.name: Mode 1: Tragic Loss
cards.power: The story must suffer a genuine, irreversible loss this turn. No jokes. No escapes.

cards.art: dodo bird slipping on banana peel in disaster of its own making
cards.lore: Things go wrong. It's your fault. Play the gap between intention and catastrophic execution.
cards.name: Mode 2: Comic Fault
cards.power: Something goes terribly wrong in the scene, and it is explicitly, undeniably your character's fault.

cards.art: salmon in tweed on penny-farthing drinking tea, completely blasé
cards.lore: The impossible is normal. Don't explain it. Coherence is optional; connection matters more.
cards.name: Mode 3: Absurd Normal
cards.power: Introduce a completely impossible, physics-breaking element to the scene and refuse to explain it or act surprised.

cards.art: corgi in cape standing on clifftop in lightning storm, absolute conviction
cards.lore: Your Character is right for this moment. Play the peak. Commit to the triumph, no matter how stupid the stakes.
cards.name: Mode 4: Heroic Peak
cards.power: Succeed against impossible, ridiculous odds with complete, unironic sincerity.

cards.art: galaxy-eyed owl seeing cosmic significance in a coffee cup
cards.lore: Something profound is happening beneath the surface. The diner coffee is actually the nectar of the underworld.
cards.name: Mode 5: Mystical Surface
cards.power: Reveal a hidden, cosmic, or supernatural layer operating directly beneath a mundane, boring interaction.

cards.art: skunk in front of DO NOT CROSS tape, crossing it with deliberate calm
cards.lore: Make the table uncomfortable in a way that serves the story. Cross the line. Sell it.
cards.name: Mode 6: Forbidden Line
cards.power: Cross the exact social or narrative boundary the current scene has been politely tiptoeing around.

cards.art: chameleon in tuxedo removing own head at microphone, new character waiting
cards.lore: Voluntary drama. A good death scene is a gift to the story. Exit gracefully so someone else can enter.
cards.name: The Character Switch
cards.power: Voluntarily kill off or eject your current character from the story to immediately draw and play a new one.

cards.art: large pink eraser wiping out entire comic storyboard, clean green space emerging
cards.lore: The Finale doesn't have to be neat. It has to be true to what everyone built. A messy ending earned beats a neat ending imported. Then wipe it.
cards.name: Tabula Rasa (The Cleansing)
cards.power: Upon Quest Collapse, wipe all Scene cards from the Stage. Send everything to the discard pile. Start Akt 1 fresh.

cards.art: chihuahua slamming giant green button with both paws, sparks flying
cards.lore: That landed. Spontaneous, no explanation needed. Laughter breaks nothing—if you're laughing, you're playing it right.
cards.name: KayfaBINGO!
cards.power: Yell this out of turn to validate another player's perfect, spontaneous narrative beat.

cards.art: gorilla on bongo drums roaring at metagamer
cards.lore: Don't say 'I deal 3 damage.' Say 'Your empire glitches and seven kinds of collapse happen at once.' Perform, don't calculate.
cards.name: KayfaBONGO!
cards.power: Yell this when a player uses game mechanics instead of storytelling. Force them to restate it as a narrative event.

cards.art: pug with exposed brain, one question mark, genuinely confused
cards.lore: Not a criticism. A question. Keep it short, keep it about the story, keep it kind. If someone is uncomfortable, boggle it.
cards.name: KayfaBOGGLE!
cards.power: Pause the game to ask exactly one concrete question about a narrative gap. The active player must answer in 1–2 sentences.

cards.art: parrot in referee stripes holding yellow card
cards.lore: A rule was broken. The fiction was breached. Nullify the progress. Call them out to protect the Kayfabe.
cards.name: Blödsinn!
cards.power: Call out a broken rule, ignored mode, or out-of-character action. If the table agrees, the Quest Die freezes this turn.

cards.art: praying mantis under interrogation lamp, all dialogue bubbles ending in question marks
cards.lore: Wer eine Aussage macht, verliert den Zug. The Quest Die drops. Active listening forced through grammatical sabotage.
cards.name: Questions Only?
cards.power: For this round, all direct narrative statements are forbidden. Every piece of dialogue and narration must be a question.

cards.art: red octopus with megaphone surrounded by genre clapperboards
cards.lore: The original was boring. Do it again, but weirder. Practice taking correction without losing face.
cards.name: New Choice!
cards.power: Scream 'NEW CHOICE!' to force the active player to instantly rewrite and replace their last sentence with something entirely different.

cards.art: cowboy-astronaut chameleon half-Western half-sci-fi, clapperboard in hand
cards.lore: Suddenly... a bureaucratic office thriller! Watch how framing violently alters the exact same story.
cards.name: Genre Shift
cards.power: Draw a random genre card. The current scene MUST instantly pivot to match the tropes of that genre.

cards.art: mole in glasses receiving absurd secret message, reading it with complete commitment
cards.lore: The ambassador has already shipped the bananas. Now make it make sense in our medieval fantasy scene. Irgendwie.
cards.name: The Blind Line
cards.power: Force a player to seamlessly weave a random, pre-written, completely absurd sentence into their monologue.

cards.art: two-faced coin (angel/devil) with gold and dark halves balanced
cards.lore: Drei Leben einer Story. Play the Deus Ex Machina, then play the total collapse. At the end, ask: which version was ehrlicher?
cards.name: Best / Worst of Times
cards.power: Force the table to play the exact same scene three times: Normal, Flawless Success, and Absolute Catastrophe.

cards.art: penguin frozen mid-gesture in ice cube, another penguin outside beginning entirely different pantomime
cards.lore: Physical pantomime as the ultimate narrative hijack. The old scene is paused; the new reality overwrites it.
cards.name: SPACE JUMP (Freeze!)
cards.power: Yell FREEZE! Assume the exact physical posture of the active player, and use that pose to start a completely different scene.

cards.art: five monkeys in telephone-game chain, panic growing with each misinterpretation
cards.lore: Stille Post mit Konsequenzen. The difference between your narrative intent and their spoken impact is the punchline.
cards.name: Chain Story
cards.power: Narrate a scene using ONLY silent physical gestures. The next player must interpret the pantomime aloud to continue the story.

cards.art: yellow bulldozer pushing colorful Stage cards off cliff into reframed reality
cards.lore: Nothing gets erased, just reframed. Sometimes the bulldozer is the only valid literary device.
cards.name: The Stage Override
cards.power: Overwrite a full Stage slot. Re-frame what was there completely. Yes-and, not yes-but-actually-no.

cards.art: badger barrister in wig slamming gavel on contract
cards.lore: Not 'Yes, and'—but 'Yes, but actually...' Dialectical thinking where conflict is the only engine.
cards.name: OBJECTION! (Yes, But...)
cards.power: Force the active player to introduce a narrative contradiction. The Quest Die cannot rise until the contradiction is resolved.

cards.art: tortoise shell divided into four vivid genre zones
cards.lore: Place it on the border. I dare you to mix Realism and Satire. Context interprets action. Consistency will be socially negotiated.
cards.name: Genre Squares
cards.power: Divide the physical table into four zones (Realism, Absurdism, Mythos, Satire). Where you place your card dictates the genre.

cards.art: magpie rearranging letter tiles on corkboard: GIVE ME TIME
cards.lore: Deine Worte, nicht meine. To speak freely, you must pay the Quest Die a tax. Wessen Sprache bestimmt die Realität?
cards.name: Ransom Notes
cards.power: Restrict a player's entire vocabulary for the session to 10 specific word tokens. They must pay to borrow words from others.

cards.art: frog in paper fast-food crown, absolute sovereign certainty
cards.lore: Final call on any argument. A crown made of fast-food paper. Most tables won't need this. Yours probably will.
cards.name: King Kayfabian
cards.power: Seize absolute, dictatorial control over all rules disputes at the table for exactly one turn.

cards.art: moose at diner counter next to hero who is complaining about the coffee
cards.lore: We are hunting a myth, but first, let's complain about the weather for twenty minutes. A masterpiece of Sidetracking.
cards.name: The Great Moose Hunt
cards.power: Begin a grand, mythic quest that immediately gets sidetracked by a mundane complaint about a coffee shop.

cards.art: rat waiter in tuxedo presenting meatballs to awkward couple at candlelit table
cards.lore: Can I have your meatballs? Do you drink alcohol? Every day. A one-minute masterclass in terrible status play.
cards.name: The Stolen Meatballs
cards.power: Force two characters into an incredibly awkward first date scenario filled with twitching and terrible questions.

cards.art: pelican doctor holding X-ray showing alien embryo, both equally shocked
cards.lore: Positive forward movement does not mean happy. Raise the stakes so high the audience can't look away.
cards.name: The Abdominal Alien
cards.power: Escalate a minor medical or personal issue into a full-blown sci-fi horror event in a single sentence.

cards.art: wet spaghetti meteor impact on forest picnic, red sauce explosion
cards.lore: Because getting hit by a ton of wet pasta is technically a conclusion. A monument to the desperate desire to be original.
cards.name: The Wet Spaghetti Meteor
cards.power: End a scene with the most unearned, absurd, gravity-defying Deus Ex Machina possible.

cards.art: watercolour explosion on blank canvas, no subject
cards.lore: [ Accuse your friends of something specific here ]
cards.name: — Blank Card #1
cards.power: [ Write your own cynical sabotage here ]

cards.art: animals with blank signs marching
cards.lore: [ Blame Uncle FrizzleBob for the consequences here ]
cards.name: — Blank Card #2
cards.power: [ Break the game intentionally here ]

cards.art: glowing white cube in pen-and-ink void
cards.lore: [ Roll D6 to suffer the consequences ]
cards.name: Mode 7: [ ]
cards.power: [ Define a new emotional cage for your table ]

cards.art: old man with QR-code eyeball giving thumbs up, warm light radiating
cards.lore: Kayfabizarro trusts you. If it's broken, fix it. If it's missing, add it. Destroy this book. Stay fluffy.
cards.name: The Final Blessing
cards.power: Scan the eyeball to download the apocalypse (Extensions, Lore, Add-ons). Kayfabizarro trusts you. If it's broken, fix it. If it's missing, add it. Destroy this book. Stay fluffy.
